# analyze_game_json_files

[← Command index](README.md)

List games whose JSON file has no files, or whose metadata marks them unplayable.

## Synopsis

```
analyze_game_json_files [options]
```

## Description

Goes through every game JSON file in the metadata repository, across all supercategories,
categories and subcategories, and logs two lists: games whose JSON file lists no
files, and games whose metadata entry does not have `playable` set to Yes.

Nothing is changed; the lists are only written to the log.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-m, --mode <All\|MissingGameFiles\|UnplayableGames>` | Which list to show: games with no files, unplayable games, or both. Default: `All`. Allowed: `All`, `MissingGameFiles`, `UnplayableGames`. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Show both lists

```bash
analyze_game_json_files
```

### Show only games with no files

```bash
analyze_game_json_files -m MissingGameFiles
```

### Show only unplayable games

```bash
analyze_game_json_files -m UnplayableGames
```
